NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The failing assertion is a test-scoping defect, not a detector defect. `AC-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-ZERO` (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/spec.xml:404-423`) pinned zero attempt-pair findings over the 26 authoring archive bundles. Its plan, D0 (`C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/plan.xml:157-195`), widened that to a dynamic enumeration of every archive bundle so the denominator could not silently shrink — a bundle vanishing from the corpus would fail the containment check rather than let the zero become vacuous. That counterweight is right, but the widened assertion also became a promise that no future delivery may ever carry a live attempt-pair finding, which the product does not promise and should not.
The promise is now false for an honest reason. Whole-population measurement on 2026-10-01 found 163 archive directories with exactly one live finding — `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6`, T-005 events 14→15, id `792aa42b0c989c73` — and zero retired-code findings. The finding's chronology claim was withdrawn and the result acknowledged, but the immutable attempt events remain and the detector correctly raises. Rewriting the events or muting the detector to make the suite green would trade a real signal for a green check; that is the failure mode the corpus regression exists to catch, inverted.
The freeze is taken from a verifiable past state, not from today's whole archive. Historical close commit `20b9135b47771b66efebe40709dd7c777936d901` contains exactly 27 `C-*` archive bundles: the 26 `AUTHORING_ARCHIVE_C_IDS` plus `C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY` itself. Rescoring all 27 on 2026-10-01 produced zero live and zero retired findings, and the existing positive identical-tree and F286 fixtures pass. The 163-member corpus failure and this clean 27-member scan are different populations: together they establish the baseline failure and the selected historical baseline, but they do not by themselves prove the red direction of the new historical guard, which is a plan-time fixture duty (intact fixture passes; a missing member or a real triggering pair in a member of that same fixture fails). Freezing that membership keeps the denominator-shrink defense — every historical member must still exist — while moving the guarantee from "zero findings over every future delivery" to "zero findings over the verified historical baseline, and no retired code anywhere in the complete current archive." The complete archive is still enumerated, so the retired-code rejection remains total; only the live-zero assertion is scoped.
The change stays test-only for the product runtime. `src/review/core.ts` and `src/review/catalog.ts` are untouched, so the detector, its positive fixtures, the applied-archive reddening, the superseded/rejected/cancelled abandonment exemption, finding-id stability, warning severity, and the bound-verdict Ack machinery all keep their behavior. The retained T-005 warning stays observable through the real CLI, and the historical bound pass's Ack is not treated as clearance for today's different whole snapshot.
One non-test edit is forced. The reviewed design requires the post-archive whole-CI run `bun run validate:ci` as CloseEvidence. That command matches no default discriminating shape, so the lint engine emits `change.close-evidence-undiscriminating`, whose own remediation is an additive `closeEvidenceCommandShapes` prefix in `.ngrace-lint.json`. The file already carries three project-specific prefixes for exactly this purpose; a fourth, `"bun run validate:ci"`, is additive and removes no default. Without it the mandated criterion would be knowingly undiscriminating and would fail the `--fail-on warnings` close. Warning-free lint is necessary but insufficient: an unrelated prefix plus an `ignoredDirs` addition also lints 0/0 while shrinking the checked population, so the exact additive transformation is its own close guard (`AC-LINT-CONFIG-DELTA`), and the write-population bound (`AC-NO-SOURCE-BEYOND-TEST`) covers tracked and nonignored untracked paths, excluding only the test file, the config file, and this bundle's own arrival.
The predecessor missed this failure for a structural reason. `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6` ran `bun run validate:ci` only as the plan's pre-archive `MustPassCommand` (`plan.xml:37-44`) and its post-archive verdict ran focused commands only (`spec.xml:473-480`), never rerunning the root suite. Because the corpus test enumerates the archive directory, a pre-archive run cannot see the bundle's own arrival, and the post-archive focused checks omitted the only instrument that would have executed the corpus test over the final tree. This change makes the whole-CI run a post-archive criterion, evaluated after the close's own rename, so the final applied-archive state is what the suite sees.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the unconditional dynamic zero and acknowledge today's finding. Rejected: the Ack is bound to a change id, snapshot digest, and finding id (`C-BOUND-VERDICT/spec.xml:430-530`), so the historical bound pass's Ack does not cover today's snapshot, and the finding recurs on every run. The regression would stay red until the immutable events change, which they must not.

Rewrite or suppress the T-005 finding to make the corpus zero true. Rejected: the events are immutable and the detector is correct; silencing it would be the exact substitution of a green check for a real signal that the corpus regression was built to prevent.

Hardcode 27 as the exact size of today's archive. Rejected: the archive grows by design; an exact-size assertion expires at the next close and would have failed for this very bundle's own arrival. Membership is a required-presence check, not a size check.

Keep the whole-archive live-zero assertion but whitelist the declaration-guard bundle. Rejected: a per-bundle exemption list is a growing patch surface that hides the real question — which baseline the zero is actually over. A frozen historical set answers that directly.

Use `bun test --timeout=0` as the post-archive whole-suite CloseEvidence, which is already discriminating, and leave `.ngrace-lint.json` unchanged. Rejected for this draft because the reviewed design mandates the full `bun run validate:ci` CI entrypoint, which also runs typecheck, lint, and the validators; the narrow suite command would not cover those.
Keep `bun run validate:ci` only as the plan's pre-archive `MustPassCommand`. Rejected: that is precisely the predecessor's arrangement, and it cannot see the bundle's own archive arrival.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Broader archive compatibility and bundle-versioning redesign. Outside this repair, and it carries the maintainer's standing immediate-investigation-and-ASAP-governed-repair instruction (see `CLAUDE.md`); it is not deferred debt and is not absorbed here.

Whether `bun run validate:ci` (or whole-CI commands generally) should become a default discriminating CloseEvidence shape in the engine rather than a per-project config prefix. Deferred; the additive project config is the sanctioned remedy and keeps the engine's default set unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: A later bundle archives and legitimately carries a retained live attempt-pair finding. The historical-close loop does not include it, so the frozen zero holds; the complete-archive loop checks only the retired code, so the live warning does not redden the suite; `bun run validate:ci` is green in the applied-archive state.
A retired `review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated` finding reappears anywhere in the archive. The complete-archive retired-code scan reddens, independent of the historical-zero scoping.
A historical close member is deleted or renamed. The required-presence assertion reddens, preserving D0's denominator-shrink counterweight.

A change suppresses or rewrites the T-005 finding on `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6`. The real-CLI observability test reddens because the finding id `792aa42b0c989c73` no longer appears in the emitted report.
The `.ngrace-lint.json` prefix is dropped. `bun run validate:ci` as CloseEvidence becomes undiscriminating and the `--fail-on warnings` close lint (`AC-CLOSE-LINT`) reddens.

The `.ngrace-lint.json` change drifts beyond the single additive entry — an extra prefix, or an `ignoredDirs` addition that shrinks the checked population while lint still reports 0/0. The exact-transformation guard (`AC-LINT-CONFIG-DELTA`) reddens.

A tracked path outside the three allowed files, or a nonignored untracked file outside them, is left behind. The combined scope inventory (`AC-NO-SOURCE-BEYOND-TEST`) reddens; an ignored `.ngrace/scratch/` file does not.
